description: Final production-grade hardening pass across the rebuilt site: accessibility, performance, reduced-motion/no-WebGL fallbacks, and CI-readiness. Audit the new immersive layer against the same bar the prior production audit set (WCAG AA, no sub-24px tap targets, reduced-motion honored everywhere, self-hosted fonts, no layout shift) and make sure the new dependencies and CSP are fully consistent so the four CI checks can pass. Also ensure test invariants hold and, if site-data was restructured, that its tests are updated deliberately. Depends on FEAT-004.
steps: Accessibility sweep of the new components: every 3D/motion element is aria-hidden or has an accessible equivalent; keyboard navigation reaches all interactive elements; focus-visible outlines preserved; the custom cursor never removes focus visibility or blocks AT; prefers-reduced-motion disables lenis, the R3F animation loop's motion (or swaps to the static fallback), reveal animations, magnetic/marquee, and cursor. Confirm heading order per page has no skipped levels.

Performance sweep: the 3D hero and any heavy motion is lazy-loaded/code-split (dynamic import via ClientCanvas), dpr-capped, and paused when offscreen; images keep intrinsic width/height; fonts remain self-hosted and preloaded; no render-blocking third-party resources were introduced; route-level code-splitting is intact. Verify the hero video (if used as fallback) keeps its offscreen-pause behavior.

CSP consistency: re-read src/server.ts and confirm every source the shipped 3D/motion code actually uses (blob: workers, blob:/data: images, any wasm) is permitted and nothing broader was added; remove any speculative CSP source that ended up unused. Confirm all assets are same-origin/bundled.

Dependency + lockfile consistency: confirm package.json and package-lock.json are in sync for `npm ci`; if the lockfile still needs network regeneration, make the note in task findings unambiguous and actionable for the orchestrator/CI. Confirm no unused new dependency remains in package.json.

Test invariants: confirm src/lib/site-data.test.ts and src/lib/submission-guards.test.ts still pass by inspection (content invariants preserved, guards untouched). If site-data was intentionally restructured, update site-data.test.ts to assert the same guarantees rather than weakening them. Consider adding a focused unit test for src/lib/motion.ts (e.g. supportsWebGL/prefersReducedMotion return safe values when window is undefined) if it can be done cleanly under vitest+jsdom without flakiness.

Do a final read-through for SSR safety: no module rendered during SSR statically imports three; all window/document/matchMedia/WebGL access is guarded; ClientCanvas returns the fallback on the server.

Produce a concise summary in this feature's findings: architecture/layers, per-page rebuild notes, new deps, SSR + reduced-motion + no-WebGL fallback strategy, exact CSP changes, anything deferred, and the status of the four CI checks (all deferred to CI, with the lockfile caveat if any).
acceptance_criteria: Every immersive element is either aria-hidden/decorative or has an accessible equivalent; reduced-motion disables lenis, R3F motion, reveal, magnetic, marquee, and the custom cursor across all pages; no heading-level skips.
The 3D layer is code-split/lazy, dpr-capped, offscreen-paused; images keep intrinsic dimensions; fonts stay self-hosted/preloaded; no render-blocking third-party resources added.
src/server.ts CSP permits exactly the same-origin sources the shipped code uses and nothing broader; all assets are bundled same-origin.
package.json and package-lock.json are in sync for npm ci, or the required lockfile regeneration is unambiguously documented; no unused new dependency remains.
site-data.test.ts and submission-guards.test.ts invariants hold (or were updated deliberately with equivalent guarantees); any added motion.ts test is stable under jsdom.
No SSR-rendered module statically imports three; all client-only access is guarded; ClientCanvas yields the fallback on the server.
A clear final summary is recorded in findings for the orchestrator's PR description.
verification: Grep the whole src tree for static three/@react-three imports outside client-canvas.tsx and confirm none.
Grep for unguarded window/document/matchMedia in the new components and confirm each is behind a mount/typeof guard.
Read src/server.ts CSP one final time against the shipped code's actual needs.
Confirm package.json has no unused new dep and lockfile sync status is documented.
CI (npm run typecheck && npm run lint && npm test && npm run build) is the authoritative gate and must pass; note it cannot be run in-sandbox.
findings:
ENVIRONMENT (unchanged from FEAT-001..004, re-confirmed not repaired): INTEGRATIONS_ONLY. npm registry unreachable, node_modules has NO tool binaries, npm/node broken by a missing NODE_OPTIONS preload. typecheck/lint/test/build/dev CANNOT run in-sandbox. Everything below was written/verified type-correct and eslint/prettier-clean BY CONSTRUCTION (printWidth 100, 2-space, double quotes, semicolons, trailing commas). CI is the authoritative validator.

OUTCOME: This was an AUDIT + targeted-fix pass. The immersive layer shipped by FEAT-001..004 was already production-grade against every acceptance criterion; the audit found NO a11y, performance, CSP, or SSR defect requiring a code change. The ONLY code addition is a new, stable unit test (src/lib/motion.test.ts). All findings below are verification results.

=== ARCHITECTURE / LAYERS ===
- Capability + motion helpers: src/lib/motion.ts — prefersReducedMotion() (false on server), useReducedMotion() (starts false for hydration parity, subscribes to the MQ), useHasMounted()/useIsMounted (client gate), supportsWebGL() (false on server / on failure). All DOM access typeof-guarded.
- SSR-safe 3D boundary: src/components/three/client-canvas.tsx — renders the static `fallback` on server, before mount, when supportsWebGL() is false, when useReducedMotion() is true, and while scrolled offscreen (IntersectionObserver pause). Only reaches three via React.lazy(() => import('@/components/three/hero-scene')) inside a <Suspense fallback={fallback}>. Layer is aria-hidden, position:absolute inset:0, pointer-events:none, z-index var(--z-canvas).
- R3F scene: src/components/three/hero-scene.tsx — the ONLY module importing three/@react-three/fiber/@react-three/drei. CoreOrb (drei <Float> + icosahedron) + a 42-node shared-geometry field in brand hex; scroll/pointer via useFrame fed by a window-listener InteractionDriver (Canvas has pointer-events:none). dpr={[1,1.75]}, powerPreference low-power, alpha, aria-hidden, no external asset fetch (procedural PRNG).
- Hero fallback wiring: src/components/three/hero-canvas.tsx wraps ClientCanvas with the existing <HeroVideo> as fallback (video keeps its offscreen-pause + reduced-motion behavior). Home (index.tsx) instead uses <ClientCanvas> as a decorative section backdrop with a static CSS-gradient fallback and keeps <HeroVideo> in the perspective card.
- Motion primitives (src/components/motion/): smooth-scroll.tsx (lenis; no-op on server + reduced motion; resets scroll on route change), reveal.tsx (IntersectionObserver add-is-visible/unobserve; reduced-motion + no-IO => starts visible), magnetic.tsx (gated to (hover:hover)+(pointer:fine) AND !reduced motion; child untouched otherwise), marquee.tsx (duplicated track, aria-hidden clone, role=group+label, pause/play button with aria-pressed/aria-controls + sr-only text), custom-cursor.tsx (decorative, aria-hidden; disabled on coarse/touch + reduced motion; NEVER hides the native cursor).
- Shell/sections: site-shell.tsx (SiteHeader a11y intact: condense-on-scroll honoring reduced motion, mobile focus trap, native `inert` backdrop, aria-expanded/controls/current; PageLayout mounts SmoothScrollProvider + decorative CustomCursor; PageIntro => <h1>). content-sections.tsx (SectionHeading => <h2>; cards => <h3>; MetricsStrip count-up preserves reduced-motion + qualitative shortcut; TechnologyBand uses <Marquee>; FaqSection keeps Radix Accordion). All content sourced unchanged from site-data.ts.

=== PER-PAGE (10 routes, verified) ===
Heading order clean everywhere (no skips): home/playbook/playbook-form open with a single <h1>; SectionHeading supplies <h2>; card grids supply <h3>. services.tsx and projects.tsx use an sr-only <h2> so there is no h1->h3 jump. Legal pages (privacy-policy, terms-of-service) use PageIntro <h1> + a flat list of <h2>. index.tsx composes the 3D hero backdrop + full narrative (MetricsStrip, ProjectsGrid limit 4, PinnedServicesShowcase, TechnologyBand, IndustryGrid limit 8, ValuesGrid, FounderStory, ProcessGrid, FaqSection) inside ScrollFocusStack; CTAs wrapped in <Magnetic>. contact-us + both playbook routes keep ContactForm/PlaybookForm wired to submitContact/requestPlaybook with the honeypot `website` (aria-hidden label, tabIndex -1) and hidden `startedAt` intact — verified by grep. Every route's head meta/canonical was left untouched by FEAT-004 and remains so.

=== ACCESSIBILITY SWEEP (result: PASS, no changes) ===
- Decorative-only: the R3F Canvas, ClientCanvas layer, aurora blobs, hero floating badges, playbook cover, and custom cursor are all aria-hidden. The hero remains fully usable as text/video without WebGL.
- Keyboard/AT: honeypot input is aria-hidden + tabIndex -1 (out of tab order + AT); marquee exposes a real <button> pause control with aria-pressed/aria-controls; native cursor is NEVER hidden (grep confirms zero `cursor: none` rules; the custom-cursor's `has-custom-cursor` body class has no CSS counterpart, so it is a harmless no-op that does not affect the native cursor or focus).
- focus-visible: global `:focus-visible { outline: 3px solid var(--ring); outline-offset: 3px; }` (styles.css ~L195) is intact and not overridden by any immersive rule.
- Reduced motion: JS gates disable lenis (SmoothScrollProvider no-op), the R3F scene (ClientCanvas falls back to the static element via useReducedMotion), Magnetic, and CustomCursor. CSS `@media (prefers-reduced-motion: reduce)` neutralises `.scroll-reveal` and every `[class*="immersive-"]` element (animation:none, transition ~0, transform:none) plus the global `*` animation kill — covering reveal + marquee. All six vectors (lenis, R3F motion, reveal, magnetic, marquee, cursor) are disabled.
- Tap targets: marquee toggle carries min-height:24px; small text uses --raspberry-ink (no sub-AA brand pink) — WCAG AA bar from the prior audit held.

=== PERFORMANCE SWEEP (result: PASS, no changes) ===
3D hero is code-split (React.lazy dynamic import — three never in the SSR/initial route chunk), dpr-capped [1,1.75], offscreen-paused (IntersectionObserver unmounts the canvas), pointer-events:none. Hero video fallback keeps its offscreen-pause + reduced-motion behavior. Images still spread intrinsic width/height from @/assets/images (no layout shift; images.ts untouched/generated). Fonts remain self-hosted via @fontsource-variable and preloaded in __root.tsx. No render-blocking third-party resources introduced — everything is same-origin/bundled. Route-level code-splitting intact (file-based routes).

=== CSP (src/server.ts) — result: EXACT, no change ===
Shipped 3D/motion code needs exactly: worker-src 'self' blob: (Vite dev client + any drei/worker off-main-thread, all same-origin bundled) and img-src 'self' data: blob: (canvas/WebGL readback + generated textures produce object URLs). Both are present and minimal. NO wasm/`wasm-unsafe-eval` (three core ships no WebAssembly; no draco/basis decoders are pulled in — the scene is fully procedural), NO `unsafe-eval`, NO third-party host. connect-src stays 'self' (the only cross-origin call, the Supabase insert, is server-side). Nothing speculative to remove; nothing broader was added. All assets same-origin/bundled — confirmed.

=== DEPENDENCIES + LOCKFILE ===
package.json new deps are all USED (no unused dep): three (hero-scene), @react-three/fiber (hero-scene Canvas/useFrame), @react-three/drei (hero-scene Float), lenis (smooth-scroll), and devDep @types/three (types). Versions are React-19 compatible (R3F v9 / drei v10).
LOCKFILE — ACTION REQUIRED BY CI/MAINTAINER (unchanged, re-confirmed): package-lock.json does NOT contain three / @react-three/* / lenis / @types/three (grep => 0 matches), so it is OUT OF SYNC with package.json. It CANNOT be regenerated in this sandbox because INTEGRATIONS_ONLY makes the npm registry unreachable (no resolved URLs / integrity hashes / transitive tree obtainable), and hand-fabricating entries would produce a broken lockfile that fails `npm ci` worse than a clear note. TO FIX (single blocking item for CI green): a maintainer/CI step with network access must run `npm install` once to regenerate package-lock.json in sync with package.json, then commit it BEFORE `npm ci` (and therefore all four CI checks) can pass. Do NOT hand-edit the lockfile.

=== TESTS ===
- site-data.test.ts and submission-guards.test.ts: invariants hold by inspection (site-data.ts content and submission-guards.ts logic were never touched across FEAT-001..005). services=4, projects>=16, metrics=4, technologies=8, industries>=15, desc>80, items>=6, image truthy; rate-limit + human-timing guards unchanged. Neither test was weakened.
- ADDED src/lib/motion.test.ts: a focused, non-flaky suite pinning the SSR contract of prefersReducedMotion() and supportsWebGL(). NOTE ON ENVIRONMENT: the repo has NO vitest config and NO configured test.environment, so vitest runs in its default `node` environment (jsdom is a devDependency but not wired in, and the two existing tests are pure-node). Rather than introduce a global jsdom env (which could perturb the existing node-env tests) the new test is annotated `// @vitest-environment node` and asserts the pure server branches (window/document undefined => prefersReducedMotion()=false, supportsWebGL()=false). This exactly matches the feature's 'return safe values when window is undefined' suggestion and has zero DOM/timing flakiness. The React hooks (useReducedMotion/useHasMounted) are intentionally NOT exercised (they'd require a DOM env); their server contract ('start false') is what these primitives encode.

=== SSR SAFETY (final read-through: PASS) ===
grep of the whole src tree: `three` / @react-three/fiber / @react-three/drei appear ONLY in src/components/three/hero-scene.tsx; `lenis` only in src/components/motion/smooth-scroll.tsx. No route or shared layout statically imports three (index.tsx imports ClientCanvas; site-shell.tsx imports HeroCanvas — neither pulls three at module scope). All window/document/matchMedia/IntersectionObserver access in the new components is inside useEffect (client-only) or behind a typeof guard. ClientCanvas yields the fallback on the server. Confirmed.

=== DEFERRED / STATUS OF THE FOUR CI CHECKS ===
All four are DEFERRED TO CI (cannot run in-sandbox): 1) typecheck (tsc --noEmit), 2) lint (eslint .), 3) test (vitest run — now includes motion.test.ts), 4) build (vite build, SSR — the authoritative proof the 3D backdrop does not crash server render). Checks 1-2-4 will only pass once the lockfile is regenerated (see LOCKFILE above), because CI uses `npm ci`. That lockfile regeneration is the single deferred, network-dependent action; everything else in the rebuild is complete. Nothing else deferred.
